feed.title: appstore-spec
feed.subtitle: Documentation for the HAX appstore specification: external media providers, upload targets, reusable stax templates, and autoloaded elements for the HAX editor.

entry.title: Overview
entry.content:
appstore-spec documents the HAX appstore specification: the schema that defines external media providers, upload targets, reusable stax templates, and autoloaded elements for the HAX editor.

An appstore payload is typically returned by a backend endpoint (for example generateAppStore) or loaded from a static JSON file. HAX reads these keys at the top level via HaxStore._loadAppStoreData in webcomponents elements/hax-body/lib/hax-store.js. A payload wrapped in { "data": { ... } } is ignored.

Root structure

An appstore payload usually looks like:

Top-level keys

  • status — numeric status code (typically 200).
  • apps — array of app provider definitions (hax-app data).
  • stax — array of reusable content stacks (hax-stax data).
  • autoloader — object or array of custom element imports to preload.

example.json in the repository has a representative payload derived from current HAX integrations, and the examples/ directory has more, including an invalid/ subfolder of mistakes the validator catches.

Machine-readable schema and validation

schema/appstore.schema.json is JSON Schema draft 2020-12 with the behavior notes in this documentation embedded as descriptions. scripts/validate.js adds checks a schema cannot express, including:

  • credentials committed in data / headers
  • search keys HAX ignores
  • select options that all share one value
  • gizmo.type written as a literal instead of a path
  • _url_source without a gizmo.id
  • duplicate app titles

entry.title: Apps & Connections
entry.content:
Each item in apps is a provider definition with a details block (display information) and a connection block (how HAX talks to the provider).

details fields

  • title — provider display label.
  • icon — icon used in the HAX UI.
  • color — accent color for the provider card.
  • author — provider owner / source.
  • description — short description shown in the UI.
  • status — provider state (commonly available).
  • tags — searchable categorization terms.
  • tos — optional terms / policy links.

connection fields

  • protocol — http or https.
  • url — provider host and base path, without the protocol.
  • headers — optional request headers.
  • data — default query values sent with every operation.
  • auto — optional boolean, default true: run the browse request as soon as the app is activated.
  • operations — browse (required) and optionally add. HAX does not read any other operation names.

When the HAXcms platform setting disables onlineMedia, only apps with an add operation are loaded.

Build URLs the way HAX does: protocol + "://" + url + "/" + endPoint. So connection.url has no protocol, and an operation's endPoint has no leading slash.

Never commit real credentials. Use a {{NAME}} placeholder the backend fills in, or broker the request through your backend (HAXcms does this). site_token in data is sent as the X-HAXCMS-Site-Token header, and a HAXcms session JWT is added as an Authorization: Bearer header automatically.

entry.title: Operations
entry.content:
Operations define how HAX talks to a provider. Each app's connection.operations object supports a required browse operation and an optional add operation.

Common operation fields

  • method — HTTP method (GET, POST, etc).
  • endPoint — path appended to connection.url after a / (no leading slash).
  • data — request query values, merged over connection.data.
  • resultMap — path mappings from the provider response into HAX preview/gizmo data.

Browse-only fields

  • search — search inputs. Only the first key is used: Merlin's "Search <app title>" command sends the user's text as that query parameter. Further keys, and the legacy format / items / slot / component hints, are not rendered by current HAX, so put fixed filters in data.
  • pagination — { style: "page" | "offset" | "link", props: {...} }. Stored but not used by any HAX UI today.

Browse operation

browse is the standard operation for searching and selecting media.

Add operation

add is used for upload/create flows, for example local file upload in HAXCMS integrations.

An add operation needs acceptsGizmoTypes, or the app is never offered as an upload target. * means "files HAX can't classify," not "everything."

entry.title: resultMap & Special Values
entry.content:
resultMap maps upstream API response data into HAX item previews and final gizmo values.

resultMap fields

  • items — dot path to the array of result records. If it doesn't resolve, the whole response is used as the array.
  • preview — fields shown in result cards: title, details (HTML stripped) and id are required; image is optional, with resultMap.image as a fixed fallback.
  • gizmo — target value to dot path mappings. These become the inserted element's properties via guessGizmo.
  • defaultGizmoType — gizmo type for every result (image, video, audio, pdf, document, content, wikipedia, ...).
  • gizmo.type / gizmo.mimetype — paths whose resolved value picks the gizmo type per result (e.g. "type": "data.0.media_type"). Writing "type": "video" looks up result.video instead of using the literal.
  • _url_source — URL template; the first <%= id %> is replaced by the mapped gizmo.id, and the result becomes source and url.

Any preview or gizmo value can use the split rule to take one piece of a string:

See examples/split-id.json in the repository for a full working example.

add result maps use item (a path to the uploaded record, e.g. data.file) instead of items.

Special request values

Recognized special values

  • site_token / siteToken in data — sent as the X-HAXCMS-Site-Token header, never in the query string.
  • __HAXAPPENDUPLOADENDPOINT__: true — prepends HaxStore.connectionRewrites.appendUploadEndPoint to the query (used for HAXcms local files).
  • Array values repeat the parameter; null sends the bare key.
  • A HAXcms session JWT, when present, is sent as Authorization: Bearer <jwt> unless you set Authorization yourself. The older __HAXJWT__ placeholder is no longer read.

entry.title: Stax & Autoloader
entry.content:
Stax

stax is an array of named content stacks (HAX elements) users can insert as reusable patterns.

Autoloader

autoloader declares custom elements that should be available to HAX. Two formats are supported:

  • An object map: tagName -> importPath, or tagName -> { "import": path, "haxProperties": {...} } to ship an element's HAX definition over the wire.
  • An array of tag names, each imported from @haxtheweb/<tag>/<tag>.js. This is what the HAXcms PHP and Node.js backends emit.

HAXcms filters the autoloader by settings/enabledBlocks.json when that file exists.

Integration notes

  • Backends can serve appstore payloads from static JSON or dynamic endpoint generation.
  • In HAXCMS, provider search can be brokered through backend endpoints so API keys are not exposed to the browser.
  • For HAXCMS local file integrations, __HAXAPPENDUPLOADENDPOINT__ and site_token are the recognized special values.

Rules for tools and agents writing appstore payloads

  1. Keep keys at the top level (status, apps, stax, autoloader). Custom keys must start with x-.
  2. Build URLs the way HAX does: protocol + "://" + url + "/" + endPoint. So connection.url has no protocol, and endPoint has no leading slash.
  3. Never commit real credentials. Use a {{NAME}} placeholder the backend fills in, or broker the request through your backend.
  4. Put the text query first in browse.search. Only the first key is used.
  5. resultMap values are dot paths into each result, including gizmo.type and gizmo.mimetype. Use defaultGizmoType for a fixed type. preview.title, preview.details and preview.id are required.
  6. add operations need acceptsGizmoTypes, or the app is never offered as an upload target.
  7. Validate with scripts/validate.js before shipping a payload.

entry.title: More Schemas
entry.content:
appstore-spec is one of several schema specifications in the HAX ecosystem. Explore the others:

  • JSON Outline Schema — the content structure, site navigation, and metadata schema used by HAXcms.
  • HAX Schema — the full haxProperties contract for element authoring.
  • HAX Element Schema — the lightweight virtual DOM object format used for demoSchema, insertion, and conversion workflows.
  • Merlin Schema — the schema for Merlin's conversational options, programs, and voice/shortcut metadata.
